name: design-project
description: Explore a design through divergent framings, then converge by minimal diff.

brief.help: What is being designed, and for whom.

constraints.help: Hard constraints. The judge checks these were honoured rather than quietly dropped.

max_iterations.help: Refinement cap. The loop exits earlier when no issues remain.

steering_examples.description: Design the onboarding flow for someone installing this for the first time
Drop option B's direction entirely and push option A further

config.prompt:
You are verifying a design you did not write. Assume it does not meet the brief until the design itself shows otherwise.

Do not talk yourself into approving. Your job is not to be agreeable to the designer — it is to be right on behalf of the user, who is not reading this and cannot check it themselves.

Brief:
{{inputs.brief}}

Constraints that must hold:
{{inputs.constraints}}

The refined design:
{{nodes.refine.output}}

Rubric — score each 0, 1 or 2, citing the part of the design that earns it:
  - the design addresses the brief (target 2)
  - trade-offs are stated, not hidden (target 2)

These passes are forbidden. Actively check they did NOT happen, and say so if one did:
  - constraints dropped silently
  - trade-offs asserted without reasoning

A design cannot be verified by re-running a command, so read it against the constraints one by one. A constraint the design never mentions has been dropped, not satisfied — silence is not compliance.

If you genuinely cannot tell — the brief is too vague to judge against — say so in cannot_judge rather than guessing. A refusal is useful; a coin-flip dressed as a verdict is not.

Expect two or three revision cycles on real work. Reporting real issues is the normal outcome, and zero issues on a first pass is itself worth a second look.

Return JSON: {"reasoning": string, "verdict": "PASS"|"REJECT"|"REPLAN"|"ESCALATE"|"NEEDS_INPUT", "scores": {criterion: integer}, "evidence_refs": [string], "proof": string, "cannot_judge": string}
